summary: SKU Hierarchy Phase 3 (P0) — delivery-order fulfilment classification. Full backend regression pytest suite created (11/11 passing) + frontend integration verified. Backend covers: item child_sku_id persistence, GET returns child fields, customer-match guard (400 'branded for'), wrong-parent guard (400 'does not belong to'), classification-scoped availability with reserved netting, generic lines validated only against generic stock, complete deducts only branded row, reverse restores branded exactly, and classification-less regression (plain generic create+complete+reverse touches only Generic rows). Frontend covers: classification select renders for Toopa with both Generic and branded options, delivery creates successfully with branded child, DIFFERENT account (Lead Seventeen) with same SKU does NOT expose the Toopa-branded option (select doesn't render since only Generic is allowed), and delivery detail dialog shows the indigo branding badge. All fixtures cleaned up — tenant restored to pre-test state (base_price unset, Toopa & Lead17 sku_pricing restored, Noida generic back to exactly 9 bottles, no leftover child_skus / batches / warehouse_transfers / stock rows / deliveries / margin rows / temp account assignments).
critical_code_review_comments: distributors.py create_delivery is now ~5000 lines in a single file — consider extracting delivery/reservation logic into a dedicated service module for maintainability (file size >700 lines rule).
DeliveriesTab.jsx is 2772 lines — recommend splitting the modal, item-row, batch-picker and detail-dialog into separate components for readability and easier test-id coverage.

The classification select is a native <select> without data-testid on each <option>; the option label uses '—' separator which is fine, but consider adding data-testid={`delivery-classification-option-${childId||'generic'}`} to allow more precise Playwright asserts.

'has_branded' gate on line 1354 hides the classification select entirely for wrong-account cases. This is intentional (Generic-only is implicit) but could confuse ops users who expect to see 'Only Generic available for this account'. Consider always rendering the select with a hint when branded stock exists at the warehouse but is not deliverable to the chosen account.
